primaryKeyword: how to get a suspended google business profile reinstated
secondaryKeywords: appeal a google business profile suspension
h1: How to get a suspended Google Business Profile reinstated
metaTitle: Get a Suspended Google Business Profile Back
metaDescription: The India-specific triggers are nameable: coworking addresses, a stuffed business name, a fast category change, a service area with a visible pin.
answer: Identify the trigger before you appeal, because Google never tells you and an appeal filed against the wrong cause burns a clean attempt. Fix the violation first, then file one appeal with a complete evidence pack. Have every document open before you start — once the evidence form opens, you have sixty minutes to submit it.
takeaways: Google does not tell you why. Diagnosis is most of the work, and the answer is nearly always something that changed on the profile in the fortnight before it went.
Fix the violation **before** appealing. An appeal filed while the business name still says "Best Dental Clinic in Andheri" is a wasted attempt with a worse second one behind it.
Once you open the evidence form, you have **sixty minutes** to submit it. Scan and name every document first, or you will be photographing a shop board against a clock.
The odds are not the same for every cause. A stuffed name comes back. A virtual office usually does not, because the profile was never eligible in the first place.

sections.h2: First, work out what you are actually looking at
body: Three different events get called a suspension, and they need three different responses. Spend ten minutes here before you touch the appeal form.

The first is the profile losing its verified status. You can still see the listing on Maps, but the dashboard shows it as suspended and your edits no longer publish. Practitioners call this the soft one. The second is the profile disappearing from Maps and Search entirely — the phone stops, the direction requests stop, and searching your own brand name returns a website with no panel beside it. That's the hard one, and it's the one that costs money by the day.

The third isn't a suspension at all. A profile can vanish because a duplicate was merged into it, because someone submitted an edit that Google accepted, or because a competitor's redressal request was upheld. Check the profile's edit history and your notification email before assuming you've been penalised — if the listing is intact but the address or category changed, you have a hijacking problem, not an appeal.

Then check whether the suspension travelled. If several profiles under one Google account went at once, the account is the problem rather than any individual listing, and appealing one profile at a time will not work. Deal with the account-level cause — usually a shared address or a bulk edit — before filing anything.

callout.title: Do not edit anything yet
callout.body: The instinct is to fix everything at once — change the name, hide the address, swap the category, upload new photos. Every edit made while suspended is another change the reviewer has to account for, and a burst of them looks exactly like the behaviour that gets profiles suspended. Diagnose first, make one corrective change, then appeal.

sections.h2: The four triggers we see most on Indian profiles
body: Almost every suspension we're asked about traces to one of four causes. The useful skill is not knowing the list — it's working out which one applies to you, because Google's notification says nothing and the fix for each is different.
Work down this table and find the row where you can honestly answer yes.

table.caption: How to identify which trigger applies to your profile.
head: Trigger
How to confirm it was this one
What has to be true before you appeal
rows: Coworking or virtual office address
Search your address on Maps. If other businesses share the pin, or the address belongs to a coworking operator or a registered-office service, this is your row
Your own signage at that suite, staff there in business hours, and someone who receives visitors. Otherwise the address is not eligible and no appeal fixes it
Keyword-stuffed business name
Compare the profile name with the name on your board, your GST certificate and your invoices. A city, a service or a superlative in the name that appears on none of them is the cause
The name reverted to the one that appears on real-world proof. Do this first — appealing with the stuffed name still live is an automatic loss
Rapid edits after verification, or a category change on an aged profile
Look at when it went. If the suspension followed within days of changing the name, address, primary category or phone number, that edit is the trigger
The edit reversed if it was speculative, or documented if it was genuine — a new rent agreement, a new registration, an updated licence
Service-area business with a visible address
You have no walk-in customers but your street address is public on the profile. Common for packers and movers, home services, tutors, cloud kitchens and consultants
The address hidden and service areas declared. Google's guidelines say a service-area business should hide its address, and a visible residential one is a standing risk

bullets: Google's guidelines say an office in a coworking space [isn't listable unless it has its own signage, receives customers there and is staffed during business hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177). That sentence decides more Indian appeals than anything else in the document.

A fifth cause worth ruling out: duplicate listings for the same location, often created years apart by two different agencies. Remove or merge the duplicate before appealing, and say in the appeal that you have done so.
If two of these apply, fix both. Reviewers do not partially reinstate.

sections.h2: The evidence pack, item by item
body: The appeal runs on documents, not on explanation. A long paragraph about how important the listing is to your livelihood changes nothing; a photograph of your board with the business name legible changes a great deal.

Assemble all of it before you open the form. Google gives you sixty minutes from opening the evidence form to submitting it, which is generous if your files are named and sitting in one folder and impossible if you are still looking for the rent agreement.

Everything must carry the same business name and the same address as the profile. A licence in the proprietor's personal name against a profile in a trading name is the most common quiet rejection there is.

table.caption: What to include, what each item proves, and why it gets rejected.
head: Item
What it proves
Why it fails
rows: Photograph of external signage
That the business physically exists at that address under that name
Board not legible, name doesn't match the profile, or the shot is cropped so tightly the premises could be anywhere
Registration document — GST certificate, incorporation certificate, Udyam or Shop and Establishment registration
That the entity is real and registered at that address
Address on the certificate is the CA's office or the director's home rather than the operating premises
Rent agreement or property document
That you have the right to occupy the premises
Unsigned, expired, or in a different name from the registration
Recent utility bill
That the premises are in current use by you
Older than a couple of months, or in the landlord's name with nothing tying it to you
Interior photographs showing the working space
That customers or staff are genuinely served there
Empty desks in a coworking hall, or stock photos
Sector licence where one applies — clinical establishment, FSSAI, bar council, drug licence
That the category you claim is one you are permitted to operate in
Missing entirely on healthcare, food and legal profiles, which are reviewed harder

bullets: Name each file for what it is — `signage.jpg`, `gst-certificate.pdf`. Reviewers work fast and an unlabelled scan is an unread scan.

Expect a live video verification for anything borderline. Google's verification methods include a video call, and a request for one is neither good news nor bad — it is the reviewer asking you to prove the premises exist. Have the street, the board, the entrance, the working space and something showing you control the place, in one unbroken shot.

Appeals are decided by email and the status moves through submitted, approved or not approved. A rejection can be followed by a further review with new evidence, which is a different thing from resubmitting the same case.

body: Google publishes no reinstatement statistics, so nobody — including us — has a real success rate to quote. What follows is our own read from doing this work, offered as a judgement rather than a dataset, because knowing which fights are winnable is worth more than a number somebody made up.

The pattern is simple enough to state in one line: causes where the business was always eligible and got the presentation wrong come back. Causes where the business was never eligible do not, however well the appeal is written.

table.caption: Our read on how each cause usually resolves, and why.
head: Cause
How it usually goes
Why
rows: Keyword-stuffed name
Comes back, once the name is reverted
The business is real and eligible. The violation is cosmetic and provably fixed
Rapid edits or a category change
Comes back, often quickly
Nothing about eligibility is in question. The reviewer needs to see the change was genuine
Service-area business with a visible address
Comes back once configured correctly
A configuration error rather than a misrepresentation. The business exists and serves customers where they are
Coworking or virtual office
Frequently does not come back
If there is no signage, no staff and no customer contact at the address, the profile was never eligible. An appeal cannot create eligibility
Duplicate listings at one address
Mixed, and slow
Which listing survives is not always the one you'd choose, and merges are hard to reverse

callout.title: When the answer is to stop appealing
callout.body: If your business genuinely has no premises a customer could visit and no staffed address, the honest advice is to stop spending on appeals and rebuild around what you can win: a properly structured service-area profile from a real base, city pages on your own site, and [local citations](/glossary/local-citations) that don't depend on a pin. We would rather tell you that in week one than bill you for month three of a fight you cannot win.

sections.h2: What not to do while you are suspended
body: Half the profiles that never come back were recoverable until somebody helped. These are the moves that turn a fixable suspension into a permanent one, roughly in order of how much damage they do.
bullets: **Do not create a second profile for the same business.** This is the big one. A new listing at the same address while the first is suspended reads as evasion, and it can take the original down with it. Wait.
**Do not keep editing.** Every change is another thing the reviewer has to verify, and a burst of edits during a review is the pattern the system is watching for.
**Do not file a second appeal with the same evidence.** Identical resubmissions get closed without a fresh look. New evidence or nothing.
**Do not buy a guaranteed reinstatement.** There is no back channel, no partner escalation and no priority queue. Anyone selling one is selling the published appeal process at a markup.
**Do not change the website URL on the profile mid-appeal.** It's another moving part in a review that is already asking whether this business is what it claims to be.

**Do not go quiet commercially.** Reviews and photos stop arriving the moment the profile does, so the recovery starts from a colder listing than the one you lost. Keep asking customers for reviews; they land when the profile returns.

sections.h2: Preventing the second suspension, which is harder than the first
body: A reinstated profile carries history. The second suspension arrives faster, is reviewed with less patience, and is materially harder to appeal — so the fortnight after reinstatement is the part that decides whether this happens again.
The rules we hand clients on the day a profile comes back.
numbered: **Change nothing for thirty days.** No name, no address, no primary category, no phone number. Post, reply to reviews, add photos — all safe. Structural fields, not yet.
**One structural edit at a time, then wait a week.** Batching name, address and category into a single afternoon is the single most reliable way back to a suspension.

**Keep the evidence folder.** Signage photo, registration, rent agreement, current utility bill, all under two months old, in one place. Google re-verifies without warning and gives you days, not weeks.

**Fix the underlying eligibility, not the appearance of it.** If you appealed a coworking address by describing signage that was installed for the video call and removed afterwards, you are on a clock.
**Lock down who can edit.** Every agency and freelancer with manager access is a potential unannounced change. Owner stays with you, on an email your company controls.

**Watch for suggested edits weekly.** Anyone can propose a change to your profile, and an accepted edit that breaks a guideline lands on you. Ten minutes a week — or hand it to whoever runs your [Business Profile defence](/services/google-business-profile-optimisation).

faqs.q: How long does a Google Business Profile reinstatement take?
faqs.a: Anywhere from a few days to several weeks. A clean case with complete documents and no video verification can resolve inside a week; anything needing a call, a second review or a corrected document runs longer. Nobody can give you a date, and an agency that promises one is guessing.

faqs.q: Why was my profile suspended when I changed nothing?
faqs.a: Usually something changed that you didn't make. Check the profile's edit history for accepted suggested edits, look for a duplicate listing someone created, and check whether other profiles under the same Google account went at the same time. If several went together, the cause is at account level, not on the listing.

faqs.q: Can I appeal more than once?
faqs.a: Yes, but only with new evidence. Google allows a further review after a rejection, and that route works when you have added something real — a licence you were missing, better signage photographs, a corrected registration address. Resubmitting the same pack unchanged gets closed without a fresh look.

faqs.q: Will using a coworking address always get my profile suspended?
faqs.a: Not always, but it is the least defensible address type in India. Google's guidelines require an office in a coworking space to have its own signage, be staffed during business hours and receive customers there. If yours does all three, the appeal is winnable. If it's a hot desk and a mail service, the profile was never eligible.

faqs.q: Should I remove keywords from my business name before appealing?
faqs.a: Yes, first, before you file anything. An appeal against a profile still displaying a stuffed name is refused, and you have then used an attempt. Revert to the name on your signage, your invoices and your registration, and be ready to show all three.

faqs.q: Can I run Google Ads while my profile is suspended?
faqs.a: Search and other campaigns keep running, but anything depending on the profile — location assets, Local Services, calls from the listing — goes with it. Expect your paid cost per lead to rise while the profile is down, because traffic that arrived free from Maps is now arriving through an auction.
